question: If the resistance R is constant and the voltage V across a resistor is tripled, how does the power P change?

options.text: It increases by one-third of its original.

solution:
The correct answer is __It increases by nine times**(Option 1)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Power (P)__ is calculated using the formula P = V²/R.
 
• If the voltage (V) is tripled, the power becomes P = (3V)²/R.
 
• Therefore, the power increases by 9 times its original value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Formula Derivation:**
 
 
• Power formula: P = V²/R.
 
• If V is multiplied by a factor of 3, then P = (3V)²/R = 9V²/R.
 
 
 
• **Concept Explanation:**
 
 
• Power is directly proportional to the square of the voltage when resistance is constant.
 
• If voltage increases, power changes exponentially.
